rationale: Both passages give God's invitation, 'Return to Me, and I will return to you,' in the setting of ancestors who departed from His ways. Zechariah's warning against repeating the fathers' practices matches Malachi's indictment of inherited disobedience.
source_text: from the injustices of your fathers. You have turned aside from My ordinances and have not guarded them. Return to Me, and I will return to you,” says the Lord Almighty. And you said, “How shall we return?”

target_units.text: You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, and I will return to you, says the Lord.

Do not become like your fathers, against whom the former prophets brought charges, saying, ‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and your evil practices.’ But they did not listen attentively to Me, says the Lord.

rationale: Malachi identifies retained tithes and firstfruits as defrauding God. Leviticus declares the land's tithe and the tenth animal holy and belonging to the Lord, explaining why withholding the tithe concerns what is God's.
source_text: “Will a human defraud God? Yet you are defrauding Me.” And you will say, “How have we defrauded Thee?” “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you.

target_units.text: Every tithe of the land, from the seed of the land and the fruit of trees, belongs unto the Lord; it is holy unto the Lord.
But if a man indeed redeems his tithe, he shall add a fifth part unto it, and it shall be his.
And every tithe of cattle and sheep, and everything that comes under the staff in the count—the tenth shall be holy unto the Lord.

rationale: Malachi charges the people with withholding dues belonging to God. Numbers assigns Israel's tithes, set apart for the Lord, to the Levites for their service, showing the divinely appointed destination of those dues.
source_text: “Will a human defraud God? Yet you are defrauding Me.” And you will say, “How have we defrauded Thee?” “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you.

target_units.text: And to the sons of Levi, look, I have given every tithe in Israel as an allotment in return for their ministries, the service they perform in the Tent of Testimony.
And the sons of Israel shall no longer approach the Tent of Testimony, incurring a death-bringing sin.

And the Levite himself shall perform the ministry of the Tent of Testimony, and they shall bear their offences. It is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations. Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no inheritance.

For the tithes of the sons of Israel that they set apart for the Lord as a portion set apart I have given to the Levites as an allotment. Therefore I have said to them: Among the sons of Israel they shall receive no allotment.

rationale: Verse 3:9 repeats the charge of defrauding God and adds the nation's disastrous condition. Verse 3:8 identifies the disputed practice as withholding tithes and firstfruits, making the accusation's concrete subject explicit.

rationale: Malachi speaks of produce dues brought into the storehouses. Nehemiah recounts Levites deprived of their portions, his rebuke over abandonment of God's house, and the people's subsequent bringing of grain, wine and oil tithes into stores.
source_text: And you brought all the produce dues into the storehouses, and his plunder will be in his house. Examine, then, by this,” says the Lord Almighty, “whether I will not open heaven’s floodgates for you and pour out My blessing for you until there is enough.

target_units.text: I learned that the Levites’ portions had not been given, and the Levites and singers doing the work had fled, each to his field.
I contended with the commanders and said, “Why has God’s house been abandoned?” I gathered them and stationed them at their posts.
All Jouda brought the tithe of wheat, wine and oil into the stores,

into the charge of Selemia the priest, Saddouk the scribe and Phadaia from the Levites, and beside them Anan son of Zakchour, son of Mathania, for they were considered trustworthy; distribution to their brothers rested upon them.

rationale: Malachi promises opening heaven's floodgates and pouring out blessing. Deuteronomy promises that the Lord opens His heavenly treasure to give seasonal rain and bless the people's work, linking heaven's opening with material provision.

rationale: Malachi promises not to destroy the land's fruit or weaken its vine. Haggai turns attention to formerly fruitless vine and trees and announces blessing from that day, presenting a corresponding reversal toward fruitful land.
source_text: And I will give you instructions for food, and I will certainly not destroy the fruit of your land, and your vine in the field will certainly not grow weak,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:
whether it will yet be recognized on the threshing floor, and whether the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive trees still bear no fruit. From this day I will bless.”

rationale: Malachi says nations will call the people blessed and their land desirable. Deuteronomy describes nations recognizing the Lord's name upon His people alongside multiplied produce and livestock, joining public recognition with blessing in the land.
source_text: “All the nations will call you blessed, because you will be a desirable land,” says the Lord Almighty.

target_units.text: The Lord your God establish you unto Himself a holy people, as He sware unto your fathers, if you hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, and walk in His ways.
And all the nations of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they shall fear you.

And the Lord your God shall multiply you in good things, in the offspring of your womb, and in the produce of your land, and in the offspring of your cattle, upon the land which the Lord sware unto your fathers to give you.

rationale: Both passages accuse the people of provoking God through speech and record their counterquestion asking how they have done so. The renewed disputation introduces the complaint in 3:14-15, following the earlier challenge to divine righteousness in 2:17.
source_text: “You have made your words heavy against Me,” says the Lord. And you said, “How have we spoken against Thee?”

target_units.text: You who provoke God with your words! And you said, “How have we provoked Him?” By your saying, “Everyone who does evil is good before the Lord, and He has delighted in them,” and, “Where is the God of righteousness?”

rationale: Malachi reports the claim that serving God and keeping His observances brings no advantage. The psalmist similarly says he made his heart righteous in vain while enduring daily affliction, voicing the same temptation to regard faithfulness as profitless.
source_text: You said, “The one who serves God is futile. What advantage is there because we guarded His observances and because we walked as supplicants before the Lord Almighty?

target_units.text: And I said, “Then in vain I made my heart righteous and washed my hands among the innocent;
and I became scourged all day, and my rebuke comes in the mornings.”

rationale: Malachi reports that those practicing lawlessness are built up and survive opposition to God. The psalmist envies sinners' peace and describes their arrogant speech and prosperity, giving a fuller account of the same troubling observation.
source_text: And now we call outsiders blessed. All who practice lawlessness are being built up; they opposed God and were saved.”

target_units.text: For I envied the lawless, beholding sinners’ peace,
for there is no refusal at their death, and firmness in their scourging.
They are not in human toils, and they will not be scourged with humans.
Therefore arrogance seized them; they wrapped themselves in their injustice and ungodliness.
Their injustice will come out as though from fat; they passed into a disposition of heart.
They devised and spoke in wickedness; they spoke injustice against the height.
They set their mouth toward heaven, and their tongue passed over the earth.
Therefore my people will return here, and full days will be found for them.
And they said, “How did God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Behold, these are sinners, and they prosper; for the age they took possession of wealth.

rationale: Malachi says a remembrance book is written before God for those who fear and revere Him. Daniel describes people found inscribed in the book receiving exaltation during affliction; both connect a divine record with favorable recognition, without identifying the books as the same object.
source_text: Those who feared the Lord spoke these things, each to his neighbor. The Lord paid attention and listened, and He wrote a book of remembrance before Him for those who feared the Lord and revered His name.

target_units.text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

rationale: Malachi's book records those who revere God's name. In Exodus Moses appeals concerning God's written book, and God speaks of blotting out sinners. Both present moral accountability in terms of a book before God, with remembrance and removal as distinct actions.
